newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Smith says NZ dlr stronger than economy suggests.
newsitem.headline: Smith says NZ dlr stronger than economy suggests.

text.p: New Zealand caretaker Agriculture Minister and Deputy Finance Minister Lockwood Smith said on Wednesday the New Zealand dollar had gone above where economic strength suggested it should be.
Smith, interviewed on Radio New Zealand, was asked whether a strong dollar meant a strong economy.
"Definitely, but our dollar has gone above where that economic strength would suggest it should be," Smith replied.
Smith was making a case for fiscal prudence under an MMP environment and said higher government spending would result in a higher interest and exchange rates.

"Sure, you can increase government spending, but you'll probably have to pay for the consequences either through allowing higher inflation or higher interest rates and a higher exchange rate to try and control that inflationary pressure," Smith said.
"The markets have worked out in fact that more government spending is inevitable and that's why they see no downside risk on the exchange rate. They see no downside risk there at all.
"So they are pouring money into New Zealand to get our higher interest rates to get the benefit of that, and of course our exchange rate is going up and up," he said.
The exchange rate normally followed New Zealand's relative inflation rate.
"Ours has done that for the last 20 years, but it's now climbed above that in recent months, and that's what is putting pressure on our export sector," he said.
Smith said he wanted the present economic framework to remain in place to ensure the export sector was not damaged by excess government spending.
